Name: Net Total Flows from DAC Donors (Cur. US$)
Source_Note: Net Total flows equal gross disbursements minus amounts received (e.g. repayments of principal, offsetting entries for debt relief, repatriation of capital, and occasionally recoveries on grants or grant-like flows). Gross disbursement is the release of funds from a loan or grant to the recipient. That is generally in the form of cash, goods or services. Donor is the supplier of the resources in the form of external assistance to the recipient. It concerns only flows from DAC donors. DAC donors comprise Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Switzerland, Germany, Denmark, Spain, Finland, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, New Zealand, Portugal, Sweden and United States. Source :OECD, DAC Online Database. Data are in current U.S. dollars.

Name: Net Total Foreign Direct Investment from DAC Donors (Cur, US $)
Source_Note: Direct investment comprises financing by an entity resident in a reporting country which has the objective of obtaining or retaining a lasting interest in an entity resident in an aid recipient country. “Lasting interest” implies a long-term relationship where the direct investor has a significant influence on the management of the enterprise, reflected by ownership of at least ten per cent of the shares of the enterprise, or the equivalent in voting power or other means of control. Here, direct investors are only from DAC Countries. DAC donors comprise Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Switzerland, Germany, Denmark, Spain, Finland, France, United Kingdom, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, New Zealand, Portugal, Sweden and United States. Source_Note: Direct investment comprises financing by an entity resident in a reporting country which has the objective of obtaining or retaining a lasting interest in an entity resident in an aid recipient country. “Lasting interest” implies a long-term relationship where the direct investor has a significant influence on the management of the enterprise, reflected by ownership of at least ten per cent of the shares of the enterprise, or the equivalent in voting power or other means of control. Here, direct investors are only from G7 Countries. Source :OECD, DAC Online Database. Data are in current U.S. dollars.

Name: Net Total ODA (Official Developpment Assistance) from All Donors (Cur, US $)
Source_Note: Official development assistance is defined as those flows to countries and territories on DAC list of ODA recipients and to multilateral development institutions which are: i) provided by official agencies, including state and local governments, or by their executive agencies; and ii) each transaction of which: a) is administered with the promotion of the economic development and welfare of developing countries as its main objective; and b) is concessional in character and conveys a grant element of at least 25 per cent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 per cent). The terminology 'Net' indicates gross disbursements minus amounts received. All 53 african countries are included in the DAC list of ODA recipients. The grant element in the ODA definition is a mathematical assessment of the financial terms of a transaction or set of transactions. It is the difference between the face value of a loan and the present value (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 per cent) of the service payments the borrower will make over the lifetime of the loan, expressed as a percentage of the face value. Source :OECD, DAC Online Database. Data are in current U.S. dollars.

Name: Net Total Private Flows from All Donors (Cur, US $)
Source_Note: Total private flows is the sum of direct investment, total banks and total non banks, minus offsetting entries for debt relief from DAC Countries.  These are net flows from all donors. Official development assistance (ODA) is defined as those flows to countries and territories on DAC list of ODA recipients and to multilateral development institutions which are: i) provided by official agencies, including state and local governments, or by their executive agencies; and ii) each transaction of which: a) is administered with the promotion of the economic development and welfare of developing countries as its main objective; and b) is concessional in character and conveys a grant element of at least 25 per cent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 per cent). Other official flows (OOF) are official flows which do not meet the ODA criteria. Gross disbursement is the release of funds from a loan or grant to the recipient. That is generally in the form of cash, goods or services. These are flows from Australia. Source :OECD, DAC Online Database. Data are in current U.S. dollars.

Name: Net Bilateral Official Flows - from DAC Donors (Cur, US$)
Source_Note: Net total official flows (NOF) refers to Gross Disbursement of TOF minus reimbursement of the principal. Total official flows (TOF) include all public and publicly guaranteed flows, concessional and non concessional. It is, therefore, the sum of ODA flows and OOF flows. Official development assistance (ODA) is defined as those flows to countries and territories on DAC list of ODA recipients and to multilateral development institutions which are: i) provided by official agencies, including state and local governments, or by their executive agencies; and ii) each transaction of which: a) is administered with the promotion of the economic development and welfare of developing countries as its main objective; and b) is concessional in character and conveys a grant element of at least 25 per cent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 per cent). Other official flows (OOF) are official flows which do not meet the ODA criteria. These are flows from DAC Countries. Source :OECD, DAC Online Database. Data are in current U.S. dollars.

Name: Net ODA from Multilateral Donor - African Development Bank (Cur, US $)
Source_Note: 'Official development assistance is defined as those flows to countries and territories on DAC list of ODA recipients and to multilateral development institutions which are: i) provided by official agencies, including state and local governments, or by their executive agencies; and ii) each transaction of which: a) is administered with the promotion of the economic development and welfare of developing countries as its main objective; and b) is concessional in character and conveys a grant element of at least 25 per cent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 per cent). The terminology 'Net' indicates gross disbursements minus amounts received. All 53 african countries are included in the DAC list of ODA recipients. These are net flows from African Development Bank. Source :OECD, DAC Online Database. Data are in current U.S. dollars.

Source_Note: 'Employment is defined as a work performed for pay or profit. The value is obtained by summing up the number of employed in all manufacturing activities. Sources: Employment data are updated annually in UNIDO database

Name: % of women in local governments
Source_Note: Women’s share of positions defined according to the International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO-88) to include legislators, senior government officials, traditional chiefs and heads of villages, senior officials of special interest organizations, corporate managers, directors and chief executives, production and operations department managers and other department and general managers. Source: UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: % of women at the ministerial level
Source_Note: Defined according to each state’s definition of a national executive and may include women serving as ministers and vice-ministers and those holding other ministerial positions, including parliamentary secretaries. Source: UNDP, Human Development Reports.
Unit: % of women at the ministerial level

Name: Proportion of seats held by women in national parliaments
Source_Note: Women in parliaments are the percentage of parliamentary seats in a single or lower chamber held by women. Sources: World Development Indicators WDI, Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) (www.ipu.org).

Name: Proportion of seats held by women in national parliament (%)
Source_Note: Women in parliaments are the percentage of parliamentary seats in a single or lower chamber occupied by women. Sources: United Nations, Women's Indicators and Statistics database; and UNDP, Human Development Reports

Name: AIDS estimated deaths (UNAIDS estimates)
Source_Note: Estimated number of adults and children who died due to AIDS. Source : UNAIDS Estimates

Name: Percentage of Adults (aged 15-49) living with HIV/AIDS
Source_Note: Estimated percentage of the adult population aged 15-49 living with HIV/AIDS. These estimates include all people with HIV infection, whether or not they have developed symptoms of AIDS, alive at the end of the year. Source: United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) Global HIV/AIDS Epidemic. EPIAIDS update, December 2007

Name: Mortality rate, under-5 (per 1,000)
Source_Note: Under-5 mortality rate is the probability that a newborn baby will die before reaching age five, if subject to current age-specific mortality rates. The probability is expressed as a rate per 1,000. Sources: United Nations Population Division and  ADB Statistics Department

Name: Improved water source, rural (% of rural population with access)
Source_Note: Access to an improved water source refers to the percentage of the rural population with reasonable access to an adequate amount of water from an improved source, such as a household connection, public standpipe, borehole, protected well or spring, and rainwater collection. Unimproved sources include vendors, tanker trucks, and unprotected wells and springs. Reasonable access is defined as the availability of at least 20 liters a person a day from a source within one kilometer of the dwelling. Sources: World Health Organization and United Nations Children's Fund.

Name: Improved water source, (% of total population with access)
Source_Note: Access to an improved water source refers to the percentage of the population with reasonable access to an adequate amount of water from an improved source, such as a household connection, public standpipe, borehole, protected well or spring, and rainwater collection. Unimproved sources include vendors, tanker trucks, and unprotected wells and springs. Reasonable access is defined as the availability of at least 20 liters a person a day from a source within one kilometer of the dwelling. Sources: World Health Organization and United Nations Children's Fund

Name: Improved water source, urban (% of urban population with access)
Source_Note: Access to an improved water source refers to the percentage of the urban population with reasonable access to an adequate amount of water from an improved source, such as a household connection, public standpipe, borehole, protected well or spring, and rainwater collection. Unimproved sources include vendors, tanker trucks, and unprotected wells and springs. Reasonable access is defined as the availability of at least 20 liters a person a day from a source within one kilometer of the dwelling. Sources: World Health Organization and United Nations Children's Fund, Meeting the MDG Water and Sanitation Target (http://www.unicef.org/wes/mdgreport).

Name: prevalence of HIV, females (% ages 15-24)
Source_Note: NULL

Name: prevalence of HIV, males (% ages 15-24)
Source_Note: NULL

Name: Adults (ages 15+) and children (0-14 years) living with HIV
Source_Note: Estimated number of adults and children living with HIV. Adults are those 15 years and over while Children are defined as those aged 0–14 years. Source: UNAIDS Estimates

Name: Immunization coverage, BCG (% of one-year-old children)
Source_Note: Child immunization measures the percentage of children under one year of age who received BCG vaccination with an antigen or a serum containing specific antibodies against tuberculosis. Source: World Health Organization.

Name: Immunization, DPT (% of children)
Source_Note: Child immunization measures the percentage of children under one age who received three doses DPT of vaccine. Source: World Health Organization.

Name: Immunization, measles (% of children)
Source_Note: Child immunization measures the percentage of children ages 12-23 months who received vaccinations before 12 months or at any time before the survey. A child is considered adequately immunized against measles after receiving one dose of vaccine. Source: World Health Organization.

Name: Access to health services (%)
Source_Note: Access to health services refers to the percentage of the population that can reach appropriate local health services by the local means of transport in no more than one hour.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Number of hospital beds
Source_Note: The number of setup hospital beds available in an institution or region. Source World Bank, WDI and country reports

Name: Net migration
Source_Note: Net migration is the net average annual number of migrants during the period, that is, the annual number of immigrants less the annual number of emigrants, including both citizens and noncitizens. Data are five-year estimates. Source: United Nations Population Division, World Population Prospects.

Name: The Number of people who are undernourished
Source_Note: Undernourished People whose food intake is chronically insufficient to meet their minimum energy requirements. Source: UNDP, Human Development Reports

Name: Daily Protein supply (per capita)
Source_Note: Is the protein content of net supply of food as defi ned above. Requirements for all countries, established by the US Department of Agriculture, provide for minimum allowances of 60 grams of total protein per day and 20 grams of animal pulse protein. Source :FAO

Name: Adolescent fertility rate (births per 1,000 women age 15-19)
Source_Note: Adolescent fertility rate is the number of births per 1,000 women ages 15-19. Source: United Nations Population Division

Name: Hospital beds (per 100,000 people)
Source_Note: Hospital beds include inpatient beds available in public, private, general, and specialized hospitals and rehabilitation centres. In most cases beds for both acute and chronic care are included. Sources: World Health Organization, Country Statistical Reports and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Number of health centres
Source_Note: The number of health centre available in an institution or region. Source World Bank, WDI and country reports

Name: Healthy life expectancy
Source_Note: Healthy life expectancy refers to healthy life expectancy for babies born in 1999 based upon an indicator, Disability Adjusted Life Expectancy (DALE), developed by WHO scientists. DALE summarizes the expected number of years to be lived in what might be termed the equivalent of “full health.” To calculate DALE, the years of ill-health are weighted according to severity and subtracted from the expected overall life expectancy to give the equivalent years of healthy life.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Nurses (per 100,000 people)
Source_Note: Number of professional nurses in post employed in Public Health Center fixed facilities, per 100,000 resident population. Sources: World Health Organization,  supplemented by country data.

Name: Physicians (per 100,000 people)
Source_Note: Physicians are defined as graduates of any facility or school of medicine who are working in the country in any medical field (practice, teaching, research). Sources: World Health Organization,  supplemented by country data.

Name: Prevalence of anaemia (among women) (%)
Source_Note: Prevalence of anaemia in pregnant women (% below normal) refers to the percentage of women whose blood haemoglobin level is below the WHO norm of 110 grams per litre.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Proportion of population using safely managed sanitation services, including a hand-washing facility with soap and water
Source_Note: The Proportion of population using safely managed sanitation services, including a hand-washing facility with soap and water is currently being measured by the proportion of the population using an improved basic sanitation facility. Source: World Health Organization (WHO), United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF). Website: www.wssinfo.org.

Name: Improved sanitation facilities (% of population with access)
Source_Note: Access to improved sanitation facilities refers to the percentage of the total population with at least adequate access to excreta disposal facilities that can effectively prevent human, animal, and insect contact with excreta. Improved facilities range from simple but protected pit latrines to flush toilets with a sewerage connection. To be effective, facilities must be correctly constructed and properly maintained. Sources: World Health Organization and United Nations Children's Fund

Name: Improved sanitation facilities, rural (% of rural population with access)
Source_Note: Access to improved sanitation facilities in Rural area refers to the percentage of the Rural population with at least adequate access to excreta disposal facilities that can effectively prevent human, animal, and insect contact with excreta. Improved facilities range from simple but protected pit latrines to flush toilets with a sewerage connection. To be effective, facilities must be correctly constructed and properly maintained. Sources: World Health Organization and United Nations Children's Fund

Name: Improved sanitation facilities, urban (% of urban population with access)
Source_Note: Access to improved sanitation facilities in Urban area refers to the percentage of the urban population with at least adequate access to excreta disposal facilities that can effectively prevent human, animal, and insect contact with excreta. Improved facilities range from simple but protected pit latrines to flush toilets with a sewerage connection. To be effective, facilities must be correctly constructed and properly maintained. Sources: World Health Organization and United Nations Children's Fund

Name: Births attended by skilled health staff (% of total)
Source_Note: Births attended by skilled health staff is the percentage of deliveries attended by personnel trained to give the necessary supervision, care, and advice to women during pregnancy, labor, and the postpartum period; to conduct deliveries on their own; and to care for new-borns. Sources: UNICEF, State of the World's Children, Demographic and Health Surveys by Macro International and World Bank.

Name: Low-birthweight babies (% of births)
Source_Note: Low-birthweight babies are newborns weighing less than 2,500 grams, with the measurement taken within the first hours of life, before significant postnatal weight loss has occurred. Sources: World Health Organization and United Nations Children's Fund and World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Malnutrition prevalence, weight for age (% of children under 5)
Source_Note: Prevalence of child malnutrition (weight for age) is the percentage of children under five whose weight for age is more than two standard deviations below the median reference standard for their age. Sources: World Health Organization, Global Database on Child Growth and Malnutrition.

Name: Reported cases of malaria per 100000 population
Source_Note: The number of cases of malaria reported to the Department of Health per 100 000 population (for the relevant year).

Name: Maternal mortality ratio (modeled estimate, per 100,000 live births)
Source_Note: The annual number of female deaths from pregnancy-related causes per 100,000 live Births. Sources: Countries, World Health Organisation, and Demographic Health Survey Macro International

Name: Maternal mortality ratio (per 100 000)
Source_Note: The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) is defined as the number of maternal deaths during a given time period per 100,000 live births during the same time period. The maternal mortality ratio can be calculated directly from data collected through vital registration systems, household surveys or other sources. MMEIG the Maternal Mortality Estimation Interagency Group, composed of: WHO UNICEF UNFPA World Bank UN Population Division

Name: Incidence of tuberculosis (per 100,000 people)
Source_Note: Incidence of tuberculosis is the estimated number of new pulmonary, smear positive, and extra-pulmonary tuberculosis cases.Sources:  World Health Organization, Global Tuberculosis Control Report

Name: Income share held by second 20%
Source_Note: Percentage share of income or consumption is the share that accrues to subgroups of population indicated by deciles or quintiles. Percentage shares by quintile may not sum to 100 because of rounding. Source : World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Income share held by third 20%
Source_Note: Percentage share of income or consumption is the share that accrues to subgroups of population indicated by deciles or quintiles. Percentage shares by quintile may not sum to 100 because of rounding. Source : World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Income share held by fourth 20%
Source_Note: Percentage share of income or consumption is the share that accrues to subgroups of population indicated by deciles or quintiles. Percentage shares by quintile may not sum to 100 because of rounding. Source : World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Income share held by highest 20%
Source_Note: Percentage share of income or consumption is the share that accrues to subgroups of population indicated by deciles or quintiles. Percentage shares by quintile may not sum to 100 because of rounding. Source : World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Poverty headcount ratio at $1 a day (PPP) (% of population)
Source_Note: Population below $1 a day is the percentage of the population living on less than $1a day at 1993 international prices. As a result of revisions in PPP exchange rates, poverty rates cannot be compared with poverty rates reported previously for individual countries. Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Poverty headcount ratio at $2 a day (PPP) (% of population)
Source_Note: Population below $2 a day is the percentage of the population living on less than $2 a day at 1993 international prices. As a result of revisions in PPP exchange rates, poverty rates cannot be compared with poverty rates reported previously for individual countries. Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Poverty headcount ratio at $3.10 a day (2011 PPP) (% of population)
Source_Note: Poverty headcount ratio at $3.10 a day is the percentage of the population living on less than $3.10 a day at 2011 international prices. As a result of revisions in PPP exchange rates, poverty rates for individual countries cannot be compared with poverty rates reported in earlier editions. Note: five countries -- Bangladesh, Cabo Verde, Cambodia, Jordan, and Lao PDR -- use the 2005 PPP conversion factors and corresponding $1.25 a day and $2 a day poverty lines. This is due to the large deviations in the rate of change in PPP factors relative to the rate of change in domestic consumer price indexes.

Name: Proportion of population below the international poverty line of US$1.90 per day
Source_Note: The indicator 'Proportion of population below the international poverty line' is defined as the percentage of the population living on less than $1.90 a day at 2011 international prices.  The World Bank typically receives data from National Statistical Offices (NSOs) directly.

Name: Poverty headcount ratio at $1.90 a day (2011 PPP) (% of population)
Source_Note: Poverty headcount ratio at $1.90 a day is the percentage of the population living on less than $1.90 a day at 2011 international prices. As a result of revisions in PPP exchange rates, poverty rates for individual countries cannot be compared with poverty rates reported in earlier editions. Note: five countries -- Bangladesh, Cabo Verde, Cambodia, Jordan, and Lao PDR -- use the 2005 PPP conversion factors and corresponding $1.25 a day and $2 a day poverty lines. This is due to the large deviations in the rate of change in PPP factors relative to the rate of change in domestic consumer price indexes.

Name: Proportion of employed population aged (15-24) below the international poverty line of US$1.90 per day
Source_Note: Proportion of employed population below the international poverty line of $1.90 per day, also referred to as the working poor, is defined as the proportion of the employed population living in households with per-capita consumption or income that is below the international poverty line of US$1.9. Sources: ILO, National Statistical Offices.

Name: Proportion of employed population below the international poverty line of US$1.90 per day, aged 15-24  (%)
Source_Note: Proportion of employed population below the international poverty line of $1.90 per day, also referred to as the working poor, is defined as the proportion of the employed population living in households with per-capita consumption or income that is below the international poverty line of US$1.9. Sources: ILO and NSO.

Name: Proportion of employed population below the international poverty line of US$1.90 per day, aged 15 and over  (%)
Source_Note: Proportion of employed population below the international poverty line of $1.90 per day, also referred to as the working poor, is defined as the proportion of the employed population living in households with per-capita consumption or income that is below the international poverty line of US$1.9. Sources: ILO and NSO.

Name: Poverty gap at $2 a day (PPP) (%)
Source_Note: Poverty gap is the mean shortfall from the poverty line (counting the nonpoor as having zero shortfall), expressed as a percentage of the poverty line. This measure reflects the depth of poverty as well as its incidence. Data showing as 0.5 signifies a poverty gap of less than 0.5 percent. Sources : Country Reports on household surveys; World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Poverty gap at $3.10 a day (2011 PPP) (%)
Source_Note: Poverty gap at $3.10 a day (2011 PPP) is the mean shortfall in income or consumption from the poverty line $3.10 a day (counting the nonpoor as having zero shortfall), expressed as a percentage of the poverty line. This measure reflects the depth of poverty as well as its incidence. As a result of revisions in PPP exchange rates, poverty rates for individual countries cannot be compared with poverty rates reported in earlier editions. Note: five countries -- Bangladesh, Cabo Verde, Cambodia, Jordan, and Lao PDR -- use the 2005 PPP conversion factors and corresponding $1.25 a day and $2 a day poverty lines. This is due to the large deviations in the rate of change in PPP factors relative to the rate of change in domestic consumer price indexes.

Name: Poverty gap at $1 a day (PPP) (%)
Source_Note: Poverty gap is the mean shortfall from the poverty line (counting the nonpoor as having zero shortfall), expressed as a percentage of the poverty line. This measure reflects the depth of poverty as well as its incidence. Data showing as 0.5 signifies a poverty gap of less than 0.5 percent. Sources : Country report on primary household surveys; World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Poverty gap at $1.90 a day (2011 PPP) (%)
Source_Note: Poverty gap at $1.90 a day (2011 PPP) is the mean shortfall in income or consumption from the poverty line $1.90 a day (counting the nonpoor as having zero shortfall), expressed as a percentage of the poverty line. This measure reflects the depth of poverty as well as its incidence. As a result of revisions in PPP exchange rates, poverty rates for individual countries cannot be compared with poverty rates reported in earlier editions. Note: five countries -- Bangladesh, Cabo Verde, Cambodia, Jordan, and Lao PDR -- use the 2005 PPP conversion factors and corresponding $1.25 a day and $2 a day poverty lines. This is due to the large deviations in the rate of change in PPP factors relative to the rate of change in domestic consumer price indexes.

Name: GINI index
Source_Note: Gini index measures the extent to which the distribution of income (or, in some cases, consumption expenditure) among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. A Lorenz curve plots the cumulative percentages of total income received against the cumulative number of recipients, starting with the poorest individual or household. The Gini index measures the area between the Lorenz curve and a hypothetical line of absolute equality, expressed as a percentage of the maximum area under the line. Thus a Gini index of 0 represents perfect equality, while an index of 100 implies perfect inequality. Source : World Bank, World Development Indicators

Name: Percentage of mothers breast feeding at 6 months (% of children fully breastfed)
Source_Note: Percentage of mothers breast feeding at 6 months (% of children fully breastfed) is defined as the proportion of mothers giving infants breast milk with or without water juice, or other liquids but no foods or non-breast milk before the age of four months.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Daily Calorie supply (per capita)
Source_Note: It is computed from the energy equivalent of net food supplies in a country. Available supplies comprise domestic production, imports less exports and changes in stock. Net supplies exclude animal feed, seeds for use in agriculture and food lost in processing. Per capita supplies are derived from the total supplies available for human consumption by dividing the quantities of food by the total population. Source: FAO

Name: Prevalence of undernourishment (% of population)
Source_Note: Population below minimum level of dietary energy consumption (also referred to as prevalence of undernourishment) shows the percentage of the population whose food intake is insufficient to meet dietary energy requirements continuously. Source: Food and Agriculture Organization

Name: Daily Fat supply (per capita)
Source_Note: Is the fat content of net supply of food. Net supplies exclude animal feed, seeds for use in agriculture and food lost in processing. Per capita supplies are derived from the total supplies available for human consumption by dividing the quantities of food by the total population. Source: FAO

Name: Birth rate, crude (per 1,000 people)
Source_Note: Crude birth rate indicates the number of live births occurring during the year, per 1,000 population estimated at midyear. Sources : United Nations Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Death rate, crude (per 1,000 people)
Source_Note: Crude death rate indicates the number of deaths occurring during the year, per 1,000 population estimated at midyear. Sources : United Nations Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Contraceptive prevalence (% of women ages 15-49)
Source_Note: Contraceptive prevalence rate is the percentage of women who are practicing, or whose sexual partners are practicing, any form of contraception. It is usually measured for married women ages 15-49 only. Sources : Household surveys, and Demographic and Health Surveys by Macro International and Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys by UNICEF and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Gender-related development index (GDI), Rank
Source_Note: The GDI rank is determined using GDI values.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Gender-related development index (GDI)
Source_Note: GDI is based on the following three indicators adjusted for disparities in achievement between women and men: longevity, as measured by life expectancy at birth; educational attainment, as measured by a combination of adult literacy (two-thirds weight) and combined primary, secondary and tertiary enrollment ratios (one-third weight); and standard of living, as measured by real GDP per capita (PPP $).  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Gender empowerment measure (GEM), Rank
Source_Note: The GEM rank is determined using GEM values.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Gender empowerment measure (GEM)
Source_Note: GEM refers to the relative empowerment of men and women in political and economic spheres of activity. The three variables used to measure empowerment are percentage share of parliamentary representation, percentage share of administrative and managerial positions and percentage share of professional and technical positions.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Human development index, (HDI) Rank
Source_Note: The HDI rank is determined using HDI values to the fifth decimal point.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Human development index (HDI)
Source_Note: The HDI is based on the following three indicators: longevity, as measured by life expectancy at birth; educational attainment, as measured by a combination of adult literacy (two-thirds weight) and combined primary, secondary and tertiary enrollment ratios (one-third weight); and standard of living, as measured by real GDP per capita (PPP $). Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Human poverty index, (HPI) Rank
Source_Note: The HPI rank is determined using HPI values.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Human poverty index (HPI)
Source_Note: The HPI refers to deprivation in three essential elements of human life already refl ected in the HDI – longevity, knowledge and decent standard of living. The first, deprivation, relates to survival – the vulnerability to death at a relatively early age. The second relates to knowledge – being excluded from the world of reading and communication. The third relates to a decent living standard in terms of overall economic provisioning.  Source : UNDP, Human Development Report

Name: Mortality rate, infant (per 1,000 live births)
Source_Note: Infant mortality rate is the number of deaths of infants under one year of age, per 1,000 live births in a given year. Sources : United Nations Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Mortality rate, infant, female (per 1,000 live births)
Source_Note: Female 'Infant mortality rate is the number of deaths of males under one year of age, per 1,000 live births in a given year. Sources : United Nations Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Mortality rate, infant, Male (per 1,000 live births)
Source_Note: Male 'Infant mortality rate is the number of deaths of males under one year of age, per 1,000 live births in a given year. Sources : United Nations Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Life expectancy at birth, female (years)
Source_Note: Life expectancy at birth indicates the number of years a newborn infant would live if prevailing patterns of mortality at the time of its birth were to stay the same throughout its life. Sources : United Nations Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Life expectancy at birth, Ratio of female to Male
Source_Note: Ratio of female life expectancy at birth to male life expectancy at birth. Source: UN Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Life expectancy at birth, total (years)
Source_Note: Life expectancy at birth indicates the number of years a newborn infant would live if prevailing patterns of mortality at the time of its birth were to stay the same throughout its life. Source : Sources : United Nations Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Life expectancy at birth, male (years)
Source_Note: Life expectancy at birth indicates the number of years a newborn infant would live if prevailing patterns of mortality at the time of its birth were to stay the same throughout its life. Sources : United Nations Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Rate of Natural Increase (%)
Source_Note: Rate of Natural Increase is the difference between crude birth and crude death rates expressed as a percentage. Sources : UN population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Sex ratio (Males per 100 females)
Source_Note: Sex ratio is the number of males per 100 females in a population. Source : UN population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Singulate Mean Age at first marriage, female
Source_Note: The mean number of years lived by an assumed cohort of women before their first marriage. Source:UN-WINSTAT

Name: Singulate Mean Age at first marriage, male

Name: Fertility rate, total (births per woman)
Source_Note: Total fertility rate represents the number of children that would be born to a woman if she were to live to the end of her childbearing years and bear children in accordance with current age-specific fertility rates. Sources : United Nations Population Division and ADB Statistics Department

Name: Survival to age 40, all (% of cohort)
Source_Note: The probability of a newborn infant surviving to age 40 if subject to prevailing patterns of age-specific mortality rates. Source : UNDP, Human Development Reports

Name: Survival to age 60, all (% of cohort)
Source_Note: The probability of a newborn infant surviving to age 60 if subject to prevailing patterns of age-specific mortality rates. Source : UNDP, Human Development Reports

Source_Note: Households headed by women refer to families in which a woman is acknowledged as the head by the other members. Source: UNHABITAT, Country Reports on Household Budget Survey
